title: From Recruitment to Organizational Management: Liepin Lily Officially Upgraded to an Independent AI Product

content_html:
Tsinghua University recently held the “Extraordinary 2026” Intelligent Economy Forum, themed “AI-Driven Organizational Leap.” The forum was jointly hosted by the Center for Artificial Intelligence and Management at the Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management, the Tsinghua University Institute for Sustainable Social Value, and Tongdao Liepin Group. At the event, the “AI Transformation and Carbon-Silicon Capabilities—‘Extraordinary 2026’ Research Report” was released, and Liepin’s recruitment AI agent, Lily, was also officially launched as a standalone product.

The report shows that, based on a survey of 760 companies, early AI benefits are mainly reflected in improved operational efficiency and better product and service quality; companies that advance employee development and AI governance in tandem generally perform better in productivity and overall business value. Xu Xin, Associate Dean of the Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management, drew on 1,060 corporate cases to propose four types of “carbon-silicon capabilities” in human-machine collaboration: automation, augmentation, assurance, and adaptation.

On the product side, Dai Kebin, Chairman of the Board and CEO of Tongdao Liepin Group, said that during Lily’s co-creation period, more than 70,000 conversations revealed that corporate recruitment needs often involve deeper issues of organizational division of labor and role design. Therefore, Lily expanded its service scope from talent search to organizational design, position setting, and talent profiling, and further connected candidate communication and office collaboration. After co-creation covering 11 cities and 263 companies, Lily was officially launched as a standalone product.

This launch reflects that AI applications in human resources are extending from a single recruitment stage to organizational management and collaborative office work, and that enterprise AI transformation is beginning to focus more on human-machine capability integration and organizational effectiveness improvement.
